propositions: Four dispatch call sites use cast() to narrow transport type but perform no runtime isinstance guard before invoking optional capability members (add_comment, set_relationship), creating a silent-failure mode when a backend lacks the capability.

An AttributeError raised by a missing capability is swallowed by a broad except Exception handler, collapsing the distinction between 'capability legitimately absent (skip)' and 'capability present but failed (real error)'.
The reconciler's capability detection is inconsistent: dispatch sites use cast() without runtime checks, while fetcher.py uses hasattr guards on the same class of optional members.

A runtime isinstance guard must be added at all four sites and missing capabilities must be logged and recorded as distinct alert kinds (outbound-comment-capability-absent / outbound-links-capability-absent) on the existing bridge_alerts channel.

The isinstance check must include a hasattr fallback because @runtime_checkable protocols use getattr_static on Python 3.12+, which does not see attributes served by __getattr__, breaking proxy/mock transports that would otherwise be falsely marked absent.
Module size constraint requires _call_with_retry to be relocated from dispatch_one.py (~796 LOC) to dispatch_apply_phases.py to remain under the 800-LOC cap after guard additions.
